nodes.name: Pyrolysis synthesis of PtCu/NC
nodes.procedure: Following the reported procedure with slight adjustment (experimental details in Fig. S15), triazine (carbon source), dicyandiamide (nitrogen source), copper (II) acetate, and chloroplatinic acid were sequentially mixed and dried in ethanol. The mixture was thermally decomposed at 900°C to form isolated Cu single atoms and Pt sub-nanoclusters anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon (N-C).

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode system

double_layer_capacitance.value: significantly higher than Pt/NC and Cu/NC

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical measurement of the prepared catalysts for HER was performed in a three-electrode system using 1 M KOH as the electrolyte. All measurements were carefully calibrated to the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) scale... PtCu/NC displays a lower overpotential of 23.5 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2 compared to Pt/C (30.7 mV) and Pt/NC (37.1 mV)... at higher current densities of 100 and 500 mA cm−2, PtCu/NC still exhibits the smallest overpotential (94.5 and 177.2 mV)... Tafel slope of PtCu/NC is significantly decreased to 35.5 mV dec−1... HER stability was evaluated at a high current density of 500 mA cm−2. PtCu/NC exhibits excellent stability over 1300 h with a degradation rate of only 3.84 μV h−1.

we constructed an AEMWE using PtCu/NC as the cathode catalyst and NiFe-LDH as the anode... the PtCu/NC+NiFe LDH configuration requires only impressive 1.93 and 2.13 V to achieve current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm−2, respectively... The stability curve of the PtCu/NC+NiFe LDH device shows 600 h at a high current density of 500 mA cm−2 with negligible degradation, and the cell efficiency at this point is 64%.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals two-dimensional ultra-thin layer structure of PtCu/NC catalyst with no obvious metal nanoparticles; SAED shows amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) characterization clearly revealed that the PtCu/NC catalyst exhibited a two-dimensional ultra-thin layer structure with no obvious metal nanoparticles observed during thermal decomposition. The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern showed an amorphous structure (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals Cu atoms distributed around Pt sub-nanoclusters with Pt-Cu distance of approximately 2.8 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further investigation with a high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) revealed the coexistence of single atoms and densely packed small clusters on the carbon surface.
The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern showed an amorphous structure (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Pt localized at atomic clusters and Cu randomly dispersed throughout carbon substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images validated that Pt was primarily localized at the positions of atomic clusters, while Cu was randomly dispersed throughout the carbon substrate (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows two broad peaks at 25° and 43° corresponding to (002) and (101) planes of C, indicating absence of metal or oxide nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed that all catalysts exhibited two broad peaks around 25° and 43°, corresponding to the (002) and (101) planes of C, indicating the absence of metal or oxide nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt and Cu contents in PtCu/NC are 1.98% and 0.58% respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry) measurement showed that the Pt and Cu contents in PtCu/NC were around 1.98% and 0.58%, respectively (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows higher ID/IG ratio indicating higher defect density in PtCu/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy showed that all catalysts exhibited two characteristic bands, where the ID/IG ratio indicated a higher defect density in PtCu/NC (Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows peak at g=2.003 confirming inherent defects; PtCu/NC exhibits highest peak intensity indicating higher density of unpaired electrons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy further confirmed the presence of inherent defects in PtCu/NC of a peak at 2.003 (Fig. 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Cu 2p3/2 and Cu 2p1/2 peaks deconvoluted into Cu0/Cu+ and Cu2+ states (wide valence range 0-2+); Cu peaks shift +0.36 eV higher binding energy, Pt peaks shift -0.23 eV lower; N 1s and C 1s show increased metal coordination defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu 2p XPS spectra (Fig. S22) reveal that both the Cu 2p3/2 and Cu 2p1/2 peaks can be deconvoluted into two components, corresponding to the presence of Cu0/Cu+ and Cu2+ states. This indicates a wide valence range for Cu (0-2+).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES: PtCu/NC shifts to higher energy vs Cu/NC indicating increased Cu oxidation state (electron transfer Cu→Pt); Pt L3-edge: weaker white line in PtCu/NC vs Pt/NC indicating lower Pt oxidation state and higher Pt 5d occupation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The shift of the near-edge position towards higher energy in PtCu/NC compared to Cu/NC indicates an increase in the oxidation state of Cu (inset of Fig. 3a). Similarly, the Pt L3-edge XANES spectra (Fig. 3b) show a slightly weaker white line (HA) intensity for PtCu/NC compared to Pt/NC, indicating the relative lower oxidation state of Pt in PtCu/NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge FT-EXAFS shows single peak at 1.5 Å (Cu-N), no Cu-Cu peak confirming atomic dispersion; Pt L3-edge shows Pt-N at 1.52 Å and weaker Pt-Pt at 2.66 Å; Cu coordination number=3, Pt scattering paths at 2.03 Å and 2.74 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3c, the PtCu/NC exhibits a single dominant peak at approximately 1.5 Å, corresponding to the nearest coordination shell around copper atoms (Cu–N).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Cu K-edge shifts +1.05 eV in 1M KOH, Pt L3-edge shifts -0.48 eV; under bias both shift lower; Pt oxidation state decreases from +1.70 to +1.58, Pt 5d electrons increase from 8.36 to 8.07 (Δ=0.29).
nodes.evidence_snippet: When PtCu/NC is exposed to 1 M KOH solution, the Cu K-edge shifts towards higher binding energy by 1.05 eV due to the charge transfer from absorbed H2O molecules on Cu sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Cu K-edge shows no Cu-Cu bonds, Cu-O/N coordination number increases 2.9→3.9; Pt-N/O decreases, Pt-Pt increases forming low-coordinated active Pt sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 5e shows that, during the HER process, no distinct Cu–Cu bond is observed in the operando Cu K-edge EXAFS spectra, indicating that the Cu atoms on PtCu/NC remain isolated and dispersed throughout the reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives higher Cdl for PtCu/NC indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, we investigated the intrinsic activity of these catalysts through double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements obtained from a series of cyclic voltammetry (CV) scans at different scan rates.
